paragraphs.text: When the honeybee population of North America and Europe began to fall sharply in the early 2000s, attention focused on the countryside. Intensive agriculture, with its large fields of a single crop and heavy use of pesticides, was widely blamed. Less attention was paid to the possibility that cities, often regarded as hostile environments for wildlife, might offer bees a refuge.

A growing body of research suggests that this possibility deserves to be taken seriously. A study carried out in the English city of Bristol and its surrounding area found that urban sites supported a greater variety of bee species than nearby farmland, although nature reserves supported the most of all. The researchers explained the result by pointing to the enormous diversity of plants in private gardens, parks and even roadside verges, which together provide food for insects from early spring until late autumn. Farmland, by contrast, tends to produce a short burst of flowers followed by long periods with almost nothing.

Not all bees benefit equally, however. The species that thrive in cities tend to be generalists, able to feed on many different plants, and those that nest in cavities, such as holes in walls or dead wood. Bees that nest in the ground, which make up the majority of wild species, are at a disadvantage in places where most surfaces are covered with concrete or asphalt. Some specialist species, which feed on the pollen of only one or two plant families, are almost entirely absent from urban areas.

The rise of urban beekeeping has added a further complication. Over the past twenty years, the number of honeybee hives in cities such as London, Paris and New York has grown rapidly, encouraged by companies that install hives on office roofs as a sign of their environmental commitment. In London, the number of registered hives more than doubled in a decade. Some ecologists now warn that this enthusiasm may be doing more harm than good. Honeybees are not endangered, and large numbers of them compete with wild bees for the same limited supply of pollen and nectar. A study in Paris found that the more hives there were in an area, the less frequently wild pollinators were observed visiting flowers there.

There are also concerns about disease. Honeybees kept in high densities can spread viruses and parasites to wild species, which may have little resistance to them. For this reason, a number of conservation organisations argue that planting flowers is a far more effective way of helping bees than keeping them.

City authorities are beginning to respond. Several have changed the way they manage public land, cutting grass less often to allow wildflowers to bloom and leaving areas of bare soil for ground-nesting species. Utrecht in the Netherlands has covered the roofs of more than three hundred bus stops with plants, creating small islands of habitat across the city. Such measures are cheap, and early monitoring suggests that they can increase the number of insects in an area within two or three years.

Researchers caution that cities cannot replace the countryside. Most of the land in many countries remains agricultural, and the long-term survival of wild bees will depend largely on how that land is managed. Nevertheless, the evidence suggests that well-planned cities can play a modest but genuine role in supporting pollinators, provided that the focus is on wild species rather than on the honeybee.

groups.label: True/False/Not Given
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Choose **TRUE**, **FALSE** or **NOT GIVEN**.

questions.prompt: Early explanations for falling bee numbers focused mainly on rural areas.
questions.explain: "rural areas" = **the countryside**. İlk açıklamalar kırsal tarıma odaklanmış.

questions.prompt: The Bristol study found that nature reserves had fewer bee species than urban sites.
questions.quote: although nature reserves supported the most of all
questions.explain: Doğa koruma alanları **en fazla** türü barındırıyor; ifade bunun tersini söylüyor.

questions.prompt: Farmland provides bees with food for a shorter part of the year than urban areas.
questions.quote: Farmland, by contrast, tends to produce a short burst of flowers followed by long periods with almost nothing.
questions.explain: Şehirde ilkbahardan sonbahara kadar besin var; tarım arazisinde ise **kısa bir çiçeklenme** ve sonra uzun boşluk.

questions.prompt: Most wild bee species build their nests underground.
questions.quote: Bees that nest in the ground, which make up the majority of wild species

questions.prompt: Companies that install rooftop hives usually employ professional beekeepers.
questions.quote: encouraged by companies that install hives on office roofs as a sign of their environmental commitment
questions.explain: Şirketlerin çatıya kovan kurduğu söyleniyor ama **kimin bakım yaptığına** dair bilgi yok.

questions.explain: "rarely found" = **almost entirely absent**; neden: yalnızca bir-iki bitki ailesiyle beslenmeleri (ve toprağın betonla kaplı olması).

questions.quote: In London, the number of registered hives more than doubled in a decade.
questions.explain: İstatistik = **more than doubled in a decade**.

questions.explain: "health problems may pass" = **spread viruses and parasites**.
